name: aggressiveness
quote: He's being very pushy about this.
description: A negative perception that someone else is threatening or energetically proposing a particular change that is not welcome. The person in question likely feels justified in these actions. If the actions don't negatively effect someone, then they are 'ambition'.
perceptions: Someone is exerting energy to get what they want.
Either the whole effort is unwelcome or they're doing it with more energy than required.
results: depends on the context and your relation to the person

guidance.description: Violence and aggression rarely come out of the blue. When working with others, it’s key that you are able to identify some giveaway signals that might suggest the mood has shifted.
guidance.attribution: PeopleSafe.co.uk -- How To Diffuse Aggression – Conflict Resolution Tips

variations.name: realized aggressiveness
variations.description: If you recognize that recent actions have been more pushy than necessary or unfairly ignoring others' interests, you may feel some regret.
perceptions: I probably didn't need to push my agenda in that way.
I may have changed perceptions in a way not intended.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way

comparisons.description: 'Attack' is the action taken to forcibly advance an agenda, while 'aggressiveness' is a label applied to someone who is perceived as negatively affecting ohers.

commentaries.quote: Some types of aggressiveness can be good. If it's seen that the intended target of your actions is beneficial and that the impact to others' interests is collateral damage, it may be forgiven. But if aggressiveness is aimed specifically at degrading others' interests, they may perceive it negatively.
It's sometimes difficult from the inside to accurately judge how best to advocate for yourself. Others can critique your actions as being 'aggressive' in a negative way.
Unnecessary aggression is not justice or strength it is human weakness and desire.
The tendency to aggression is an innate, independent, instinctual disposition in man... it constitutes the powerful obstacle to culture.
